messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: generation-service | region=us-west-2 | symptom=5xx-rate > 7% for 5m. Priority: P1. Paging emma (oncall) and eng-sre rotation.

emma (oncall): on it. joining channel. any initial context? :coffee:

raj (eng-sre): seeing tail of a bad rollout on the autoscaler job that bounced some dedicated nodes. logs show a packing error from the runtime: 
```
2026-03-15T02:02:11Z runtime ERROR kv-cache: failed-to-allocate page: OOM on GPU0
2026-03-15T02:02:12Z serving WARN request-id=... model=fastgen-v3 - fallback attempted
```

mike (ops): we had a maintenance window earlier; autoscaler config got a changed limit from 8 -> 6 by accident in the deploy PR. rolling back now.

emma (oncall): thanks. i'll start Canary rollback and take traffic off us-west-2 for non-critical tiers. olivia can you help draft a short public bulletin? need to tell customers there's degraded generation in us-west-2 and we're routing to other regions for most traffic.

olivia (comms): on it. first draft below — please edit for accuracy: 
```
Public bulletin (initial):
We are currently investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation in the US-West (us-west-2) region. Some requests may fail with 5xx errors or experience increased latency. Engineers are actively mitigating by rolling back a recent autoscaler change and routing traffic to healthy regions.
Impact: partial degradation for generation endpoints in us-west-2 (affects ~12% of requests).
Customer action: no action required. We will post periodic updates and a resolved notice.
```

sara (product): add note about dedicated instances — customers with Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 may see request queuing; recommend contacting support for urgent SLAs.

raj (eng-sre): technical addendum for comms: root cause is autoscaler limit change and subsequent GPU OOM on a subset of nodes; we are reverting config and replacing 3 nodes. estimated mitigation in 12-18 minutes.

emma (oncall): good. olivia, please include the estimated mitigation window and mention the rollback. also mark affected SDK endpoints: /v1/generate and streaming endpoints.

olivia (comms): updated draft: 
```
Public bulletin (update 1):
We are investigating elevated 5xx errors for generation endpoints in US-West (us-west-2). Engineers identified a configuration change to autoscaling limits which caused reduced capacity and GPU memory pressure on several nodes. We are rolling back the change and replacing affected nodes.
Estimated mitigation time: ~15 minutes.
Impact: partial failures and intermittent stream resets for /v1/generate and streaming APIs in us-west-2; traffic for many customers is being routed to other regions automatically.
Customer action: none required. If you have Dedicated capacity pinned to us-west-2, please open a support ticket for priority assistance.
```

mike (ops): rollback complete. starting node replacements (3/3 rebooting now). routing rules are allowing fallback to eu-central-1 and us-east-1 for non-pinned flows.

emma (oncall): monitoring: errors down from 7.3% -> 2.1% over the last 3m. latency for fallback region up ~40ms. holding for 10m to confirm stability.

olivia (comms): i'll queue the update to publish — do we want to publish the initial bulletin now or wait for the 10m hold?

sara (product): publish initial now with ETA and note that we'll send a follow-up. customers appreciate transparency.

emma (oncall): agree. publish now. i'll add a short internal blurb for SRE teams on escalation steps.

olivia (comms): published initial bulletin and pinged support. link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2802468190 (internal). reactions: :loudspeaker: :white_check_mark:

raj (eng-sre): post-rollback checks: KV cache warmup happening; one pod still OOMing intermittently due to stale model weights — evicting and re-scheduling.

mike (ops): pod evicted and replaced. node health checks passing.

emma (oncall): errors at 0.9% now. starting to prepare resolved notice draft. olivia, can you draft resolved note and a small postmortem pointer?

olivia (comms): resolved draft below. feedback welcome: 
```
Public bulletin (resolved):
Resolved: The generation service in US-West (us-west-2) is operating normally.
What happened: A configuration change to the autoscaler reduced available capacity, causing increased GPU memory pressure and OOMs on a subset of nodes which led to elevated 5xx rates for generation endpoints.
What we did: We rolled back the autoscaler change, replaced affected nodes, and verified KV cache and model weight stability. Traffic routing and fallbacks ensured most customer requests continued to succeed via other regions.
Customer impact: Partial request failures and intermittent stream resets in us-west-2 for approximately 35 minutes. Customers with Dedicated capacity pinned to us-west-2 may have experienced queuing.
Next steps: ops and eng will add a deploy gate to prevent autoscaler limit changes without a staging rollout, and run a focused postmortem with action items.
```

sara (product): add a line: "If you saw degraded behavior and need assistance, contact support or your account rep."

olivia (comms): added. ready to publish once emma marks resolved.

emma (oncall): holding until 10m stable window finishes. current time window expires at last_message_ts (approx). once we hit the window and error rate remains <1%, i'll mark resolved.

incident-bot: Update: 10m stability window passed. metrics stable.

emma (oncall): marking incident resolved. publishing resolved bulletin. thanks everyone for quick triage. please add postmortem notes in the incidents repo: /incidents/postmortems/2802468190.

olivia (comms): resolved bulletin published and customer notifications queued. support notified for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

raj (eng-sre): quick tactical action items logged: (1) add deploy gate on autoscaler count change, (2) add GPU OOM alert with per-node aggregation, (3) run a rehearse of routing failover in staging.

emma (oncall): i'll own the postmortem and coordinate the follow-ups. closing thread in 1h unless someone needs more.

mike (ops): noted. I'll roll the autoscaler change process into the ops-runbook.

sara (product): thanks team. good comms.

olivia (comms): closing out and saving templates used in /comms/incident-templates.

end of thread
